title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page works in a Gabriel–Serre localization setting. There is an abelian category M_{N_0} and a quotient M_ω of it by a Serre subcategory of 'negligible' objects. τ_{ω,N_0}: M_{N_0} → M_ω is the exact localization functor. φ_{N_0,ω}: M_ω → M_{N_0} is its right adjoint (the section functor). φ is fully faithful, so τφ ≅ id.

Step 1. Let C be an abelian category and i: C → M_{N_0} a functor whose essential image lies in the essential image of φ, i.e. it consists of 'closed' or 'local' objects. Then the adjunction unit gives i ≅ φ τ i.

Step 2. Grothendieck writes (R^*φ)(τ i) ≅ R^* i. He concludes that if i is exact (or at least R^n i = 0 for n > 0), then R^nφ(τ i(M)) = 0 for n > 0 and every M in C. So objects coming from C, once localized, are φ-acyclic.

Step 3. Next take a complex K of C, a complex L of M_{N_0}, and a morphism α: i(K) → L in D(M_{N_0}). Assume τα is an isomorphism in D(M_ω). Since τ is exact, this means each H^n(α): H^n(i(K)) ≅ i(H^n(K)) → H^n(L) is an ω-isomorphism, i.e. its kernel and cokernel are negligible. The page breaks off at 'On en conclut'.

The expected conclusion is that Rφ(τL) ≅ Rφ(τ i K) ≅ i(K). So i(K) is recovered from L up to negligible objects, as the 'saturation' Rφτ L.

The likely purpose, given the folder (divided-power de Rham complex, IHÉS 1976), is comparing a de Rham-type complex with another complex 'up to isogeny' or up to bounded torsion (N_0 possibly an exponent bound). This would let one reconstruct an integral object from a complex known only modulo negligible modules. The neighbouring pages are a misfiled typescript of SGA 7 IX and are unrelated.
errors: The identity (R^*φ)(τ i) ≅ R^* i needs justification. It requires a Grothendieck composite-functor argument: τ i should send injectives (or i-acyclics) to φ-acyclics, or i should be exact so that R^n i = 0. The page uses it implicitly when deducing R^nφ(τ i(M)) = 0 for n > 0.
The identification H^n(i(K)) ≅ i(H^n(K)) presupposes that i is exact, which the page does not state explicitly.
The page breaks off at 'On en conclut' before stating the conclusion.

ideas.what: Functors landing in local (closed) objects factor as φτ, so the section functor's derived functors vanish on their localized images.
ideas.modern_name: Gabriel localization / section functor of a Serre quotient; local objects are φ-acyclic
ideas.where_published: Related material in Tôhoku and in SGA 2 / SGA 4 discussions of localization; exact statement unsure

ideas.what: Morphisms of complexes that are isomorphisms modulo negligible objects (ω-isomorphisms), detected by τ in the derived category of the quotient.
ideas.modern_name: Quasi-isomorphism up to a Serre subcategory, e.g. 'up to isogeny' or 'up to bounded torsion' in crystalline / de Rham–Witt theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; used by Illusie, Ekedahl, Berthelot–Ogus in the isogeny categories of crystalline cohomology

deep.surprise_reason: Routine homological-algebra lemma about Serre localization, written as a working tool, probably for comparing de Rham-type complexes up to negligible torsion. Nothing beyond standard Gabriel localization theory.

'L^· un complexe de M' should be 'L^· un complexe de M_{N_0}' (the subscript is partly struck or overwritten in the image).
'Un cas intéressant [?] au = cas particulier qui avant [?]' probably reads 'Un cas intéressant est le cas particulier qui précède/suivant'; it is illegible in part.
The last lines read 'soit un ω-iso[morphisme] i.e. noyau et conoyau sont négligeables. On en conclut'.
